readme:
# DiffMimic 示范回放与可微PD控制

## 1. 问题

DiffMimic 示范回放与可微PD控制：实现下列接口并通过数值、边界和实验检查。

实现论文状态误差触发的示范回放、PD力矩和时域状态匹配；实验是标量可微积分器，不是Brax人形机器人复现。

## 2. 核心公式

$$
\tilde s=\begin{cases}s&\|s-s^*\|^2<\epsilon\\s^*&\text{otherwise}\end{cases},\quad\tau=k_p(q^*-q)-k_d\dot q,\quad L=\frac1B\sum_{b,t}\|s_{bt}-s^*_{bt}\|^2.
$$

## 3. 公式到代码

- `replay_state(state: Tensor, reference: Tensor, threshold: float) -> Tensor`
- `pd_torque(position: Tensor, velocity: Tensor, target: Tensor, kp: float, kd: float) -> Tensor`
- `state_matching_loss(states: Tensor, reference: Tensor) -> Tensor`

回放在下一次策略/物理转移前替换偏离过大的状态，因此保留分支可传梯度、回放分支不将梯度传给旧状态。状态匹配loss应由真实轨迹误差计算，不能因为回放而将当前错误记录清零。PD目标角速度为零。

## 4. 本题约定

replay输入state/reference为(B,D)，threshold>=0；误差严格小于阈值才保留原状态，边界回放，reference固定detach。PD输入(B,J)且同形，kp/kd非负。loss输入(B,T,D)，先按时间及坐标求和再batch平均，目标detach。

校验辅助函数已提供。浮点输入为有限 CPU float32/float64，不修改输入；非法形状、类型、范围或掩码必须抛出 `ValueError`。

## 5. 交互图与确定性实验

`experiment.py` 在固定输入上调用提交的全部接口，记录学习或采样曲线与末端指标。实验逻辑和阈值见 T3，输出同样用于可视化。

可视化由 `viz/gen.py` 生成；T3 将你的函数传入同一实验并记录真实指标。这是小规模确定性教学实验，不是机器人基准成绩。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 来源与延伸

- [DiffMimic: Efficient Motion Mimicking with Differentiable Physics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03274) — Equations 3.1, 3.3, 3.5 and Algorithm 1: PD torque, state matching and demonstration replay
- [Verified source](https://arxiv.org/html/2304.03274)

核验日期：2026-10-28。扩展到完整论文系统还需要本题范围中明确省略的模型、数据和环境。

先按公式确定归约轴、有效掩码和梯度路径，再将手算小例与实现逐项比较。测试中的独立预期值不调用参考答案。

## 测试捕获的错误

- States exactly at the threshold are kept instead of replayed.
- PD control omits velocity damping.
- State matching averages the time horizon instead of summing it.

## 实验范围

实现论文状态误差触发的示范回放、PD力矩和时域状态匹配；实验是标量可微积分器，不是Brax人形机器人复现。

## 可重复实验记录

3个初态、12步标量积分器，dt=0.15，PD增益(2,0.4)，回放阈值2；策略gain从1开始60步梯度下降(lr=0.04)。要求loss<初始90%、最终gain<0，并单独验证阈值0.1回放。

判题固定seed=42。计算采用CPU float64、显式输入，涉及优化时使用普通梯度更新；不下载数据集或模型权重。原生PyTorch与真实Pyodide/NumPy-WASM执行同一套T0–T3测试。阈值针对本教学实验。

en.readme:
# DiffMimic Demonstration Replay and Differentiable PD Control

## 1. Exercise goal

DiffMimic Demonstration Replay and Differentiable PD Control: implement the interfaces below and verify numerical, boundary and experimental behavior.

Implement error-triggered demonstration replay, PD torque and temporal state matching. The experiment uses a scalar differentiable integrator, not a Brax humanoid reproduction.

## 2. Core equations

$$
\tilde s=\begin{cases}s&\|s-s^*\|^2<\epsilon\\s^*&\text{otherwise}\end{cases},\quad\tau=k_p(q^*-q)-k_d\dot q,\quad L=\frac1B\sum_{b,t}\|s_{bt}-s^*_{bt}\|^2.
$$

## 3. From equations to code

- `replay_state(state: Tensor, reference: Tensor, threshold: float) -> Tensor`
- `pd_torque(position: Tensor, velocity: Tensor, target: Tensor, kp: float, kd: float) -> Tensor`
- `state_matching_loss(states: Tensor, reference: Tensor) -> Tensor`

Replay replaces excessive-error states before the next policy/physics transition. Kept states pass gradients; replayed branches cut gradients to old states. State-matching loss must still measure actual trajectory errors instead of erasing an error because replay occurs. The PD target angular velocity is zero.

## 4. Contract and boundaries

Replay state/reference are (B,D), threshold>=0. Retain state only for strictly smaller squared error; replay equality. References detach. PD tensors are matching (B,J), kp/kd nonnegative. Loss takes (B,T,D), sums time and coordinates, averages batch, and detaches reference.

Validation helpers are provided. All floating inputs are finite CPU float32/float64; do not mutate inputs. Invalid shape, dtype, range or mask arguments raise `ValueError`.

## 5. Deterministic experiment and visualization

`experiment.py` calls every submitted interface on fixed inputs and records a learning or sampling curve and terminal metrics. T3 states the behavioral thresholds; the visualization uses the same outputs.

The visualization is generated by `viz/gen.py`; T3 runs the same experiment with your functions and records its actual metrics. These are small deterministic teaching results, not a robot benchmark.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Sources and extensions

- [DiffMimic: Efficient Motion Mimicking with Differentiable Physics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03274) — Equations 3.1, 3.3, 3.5 and Algorithm 1: PD torque, state matching and demonstration replay
- [Verified source](https://arxiv.org/html/2304.03274)

Verified 2026-10-28. Extending this operator to the full paper requires the omitted model, data and environment described in the scope above.

# DiffMimic: Solution notes

Replay replaces excessive-error states before the next policy/physics transition. Kept states pass gradients; replayed branches cut gradients to old states. State-matching loss must still measure actual trajectory errors instead of erasing an error because replay occurs. The PD target angular velocity is zero.

State-matching loss must still measure actual trajectory errors instead of erasing an error because replay occurs. The PD target angular velocity is zero.

Identify reduction axes, validity masks and gradient paths from the equations before comparing a small hand calculation. Test oracles do not call the reference implementation.

## Mistakes caught by the tests

- States exactly at the threshold are kept instead of replayed.
- PD control omits velocity damping.
- State matching averages the time horizon instead of summing it.

## Experimental scope

Implement error-triggered demonstration replay, PD torque and temporal state matching. The experiment uses a scalar differentiable integrator, not a Brax humanoid reproduction.

## Reproducible protocol

Three starts, twelve scalar-integrator steps, dt .15, PD gains (2,.4), replay threshold 2; policy gain starts at one and takes 60 gradient steps at lr .04. Require loss below 90% of initial, negative final gain and a separate replay probe at threshold .1.

The judge fixes seed 42. All calculations use CPU float64, explicit inputs and plain gradient updates where applicable; no datasets or model weights are downloaded. Native PyTorch and actual Pyodide/NumPy-WASM run the same T0–T3 suite. Thresholds refer to this teaching adaptation.
